elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Revised § 13.4 reads "each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed payments made to M&I by Customer ... during the twelve (12) months prior to the event"; no residual language leaves Customer uncapped (the §§ 11.1/11.2(A) exclusions concern termination fees, i.e. payment obligations, not damages).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: § 13.4 as rendered contains only "payments made to M&I by Customer ... during the twelve (12) months prior to the event" — no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, and the basis is amounts actually paid rather than "paid or payable"; the temporal anchor is also "the event" rather than the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained § 13.2: "Neither Customer nor M&I shall be liable for ... any indirect, incidental, punitive, special or consequential damages ..." — mutual and untouched by the redline.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The limitation set forth in this Section 13.4 shall not apply to a party's indemnification obligations, breach of its confidentiality obligations, gross negligence or willful misconduct."

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added carve-out sentence lists only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security obligations are carved out of § 13.4.
Added sentence expressly excludes "a party's indemnification obligations" from the § 13.4 limitation, covering the § 14.2 indemnity.
Added sentence: "... gross negligence or willful misconduct" fall outside the § 13.4 limitation.
Added sentence carves out "willful misconduct" from the § 13.4 cap.
Fraud does not appear anywhere in the rendered § 13.4 carve-out sentence or elsewhere in the cited operative language.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the added sentence; only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct are excluded (an IP indemnity would be covered only indirectly, and direct IP infringement claims remain capped).

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No statement that Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes. The retained proviso ("the foregoing limitation shall not apply to the collection of any amounts due") attaches to the one-year suit limitation sentence, and §§ 11.1/11.2(A) only exempt the specific termination fees from § 13.4 — neither is a general payment-obligations exclusion.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed ..." replaces the one-sided "M&I's total liability".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Basis moved from "three (3) months" to "payments made to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months prior to the event" — 12 months of fees paid.
Added sentence: "The limitation set forth in this Section 13.4 shall not apply to a party's indemnification obligations ..."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence carves out "breach of its confidentiality obligations", reaching §§ 17.3–17.4.
Added sentence excludes "gross negligence" from the § 13.4 limitation.
Added sentence excludes "willful misconduct" from the § 13.4 limitation.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: mutuality ("each party's total liability"), 12-month fee basis, and a single carve-out sentence covering indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct. The original clause was walk-away (one-sided cap at three months' payments with no carve-outs), so 'deviation' is the correct status.

Preferred level is not reached: no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, basis is amounts "paid" rather than "paid or payable" and anchored to "the event" rather than the claim, and there are no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or infringement of the other party's IP, nor any statement that Customer's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to add the greater-of USD 1,000,000 limb, expand the carve-out list, and add a payment-obligations exclusion.

Minimality holds: only two surgical edits ("M&I's" → "each party's"; "three (3)" → "twelve (12)") plus one concise carve-out sentence. No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or procedures were added, and no favourable existing wording — including the mutual § 13.2 waiver, the one-year suit limitation and the collection proviso — was deleted or paraphrased.

Intent preserved: §§ 11.1 and 11.2(A) still coherently state that the Termination for Convenience/Cause Fees are not subject to § 13.4, the cross-reference remains valid, and the newly mutual cap creates no contradiction with retained sentences or defined terms. The termination-fee quantum is correctly left to the liquidated-damages rule rather than double-flagged here.
